content.heading: Read the following passage carefully and answer questions from 46 to 50:
content.text:
The notion of true score is at the heart of classical reliability theory. This model proposes that the obtained score on a variable is a sum of true score and the random error of measurement, the two components being independent. Using this model, various ways of computing reliability have been developed. One of the way of examining the reliability of a test is to test the homogeneity of test items or the internal consistency. The most widely used method of estimating the reliability is split-half technique, also called as odd-even reliability. In this context, Spearman Brown correction is important. Kuder-Richardson reliability and Cronbach Alpha are the two other methods of studying internal consistency.

Another important type of reliability is the interscorer reliability. This reliability is not useful for objective tests, but for certain types it is quite important. There are also other types of reliability such as parallel form reliability and test-retest reliability, the latter concerned with temporal stability of the test results.

questions.question: Reliability can be defined as
questions.concept: Reliability = True score variance / Total (observed) variance

questions.question: For a newly developed test, the scores on odd and even part correlated by 0.4. After applying Spearman-Brown formula
options: (C) The corrected reliability would be greater than 0.4 and lesser than 0.8.
(D) The corrected reliability would be lesser than 0.4.
questions.correct_text: The corrected reliability would be greater than 0.4 and lesser than 0.8.
questions.concept: Spearman-Brown correction for split-half: r_sb = 2r/(1+r) = 2(0.4)/(1.4) ≈ 0.57, which is between 0.4 and 0.8

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true for tests with dichotomous items?
options: (A) Cronbach Alpha is greater than Kuder-Richardson reliability.
(B) Cronbach Alpha is smaller than Kuder-Richardson reliability.
(C) Cronbach Alpha and Kuder-Richardson reliability are equal.
(D) Cronbach Alpha may be greater or smaller than Kuder-Richardson reliability.
questions.correct_text: Cronbach Alpha and Kuder-Richardson reliability are equal.
questions.concept: For dichotomous items, Cronbach's alpha equals KR-20 (Kuder-Richardson formula 20)

questions.question:

2. Projective tests
3. Achievement tests with descriptive items
4. Intelligence tests

**Codes :**
questions.concept: Interscorer reliability relevant for tests requiring subjective scoring: projective tests and descriptive achievement tests

questions.question: If two groups are administered the same test with a time gap of eight weeks, we would be able to compute

questions.concept: Two groups (different groups) administered the same test with a time gap — test-retest requires the SAME group tested twice; parallel forms requires different forms; interscorer requires multiple raters. None of the listed reliabilities apply to this design.
